days.guide: Compare Van Gogh's 'Sunflowers' with another sunflower painting; talk about color choices.

questions.q: What colors did Van Gogh mostly use?
questions.a: Yellows, oranges and browns (warm colors).

days.guide: Clap ta (one sound per beat) and ti-ti (two quick sounds per beat); read 4-beat cards.

questions.a: Two sounds on one beat.
Clap, clap, clap-clap (quick), clap.

days.guide: Write a 4-beat rhythm using ta and ti-ti.

questions.q: How many beats in your rhythm?
questions.a: Four.

days.guide: Play your rhythm on a drum and show the color wheel.

questions.q: Which colors are across from each other: red and ___?
questions.a: Green.

weeks.assessment_key: Color wheel: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple in order, with each secondary between its parents. Rhythm reading: claps 4-beat cards correctly (ta = 1 sound on a beat; ti-ti = 2 even sounds on a beat). Proficient = wheel in correct order + 3 of 4 cards correct.

weeks.prep: Crayons or watercolors, paper; rhythm cards including the quarter rest.
misconceptions: Thinking a rest means stopping the music: a rest is a silent beat that still counts.
Thinking colors don't change feelings: warm colors feel energetic/happy; cool feel calm/sad.

days.guide: Sort crayons into warm (red, orange, yellow) and cool (blue, green, purple).

questions.a: Red, orange, yellow.
Calm, quiet, cold, peaceful.

days.guide: Paint a sunny day with warm colors and a rainy day with cool colors.

questions.q: Why use cool colors for a rainy day?
questions.a: They feel calm, cold and gloomy, like rain.

days.guide: Teach the quarter rest: one silent beat. Clap rhythms like ta ta rest ta.

questions.q: What do you do on a rest?
questions.a: Stay silent for one beat (hands apart).

days.guide: Clap a 4-beat 'question'; your child claps a different 4-beat 'answer.'

questions.q: Must your answer be the same as my question?
questions.a: No, it is different but the same length (4 beats).

days.guide: Your child explains how color changed the mood.

questions.q: How did warm colors make the sunny picture feel?
questions.a: Warm, happy and bright.

weeks.assessment_key: Mood paintings: sunny day mostly warm colors (red, orange, yellow); rainy day mostly cool colors (blue, green, purple). Question-answer: claps a 4-beat question and a different 4-beat answer keeping the beat. Proficient = correct color families + steady 8 beats.

weeks.prep: White, black, blue and red paint, paper strips, brushes; Chrome Music Lab 'Rhythm' (musiclab.chromeexperiments.com).
misconceptions: Mixing up tint and shade: tint adds white (lighter), shade adds black (darker).
Adding too much black at once: add tiny amounts; black is strong.

days.guide: Paint pure blue, then add a little white each step to make 4-5 lighter tints.

questions.a: A color with white added; it gets lighter.

days.guide: Paint pure red, then add a tiny bit of black each step to make darker shades.

questions.a: A color with black added; it gets darker.

days.guide: Make rhythms on Chrome Music Lab Rhythm; describe what you hear.

questions.q: What happens when you add more beats?
questions.a: More sounds play in the pattern.

days.guide: Write an 8-beat rhythm with ta, ti-ti and rest; perform with claps/pats.

questions.q: How many beats is a rest worth?
questions.a: One beat (silent).

days.guide: Perform the composition and explain the ladders.

questions.q: How did you make light blue?
questions.a: Added white to blue (a tint).

weeks.assessment_key: Color ladders: blue tint ladder gets lighter step by step (white added); red shade ladder gets darker step by step (black added). Composition: 8 beats using ta, ti-ti and rest, performed on body percussion with a steady beat. Proficient = both ladders show gradual change + 8 correct beats.

weeks.prep: Colored paper, scissors, glue, large background paper; image of Matisse's 'The Snail' (Tate); rhythm bingo cards.
misconceptions: Thinking collage must look realistic: Matisse's 'The Snail' uses shapes and color to suggest the spiral.
Reading ti-ti as two separate beats: it shares one beat.

days.guide: Look at Matisse's 'The Snail'; find warm and cool colors and the spiral arrangement.

questions.a: He cut shapes from painted paper and arranged them (a cut-paper collage).

questions.q: What shape do the pieces make together?
questions.a: A spiral, like a snail shell.

days.guide: Cut shapes from warm and cool paper and arrange a Matisse-style collage.

questions.a: Art made by gluing pieces of paper or materials onto a background.

days.guide: Play rhythm bingo: clap a card; your child finds it.

questions.q: Which card has a silent beat?
questions.a: The one with a quarter rest.

days.guide: Have your child read and clap 4 rhythm cards.

questions.a: Clap-clap (quick), clap, silent, clap.

days.guide: Your child describes the collage with color words.

questions.q: Describe your collage using color words.
questions.a: Uses words like warm, cool, primary, secondary, bright.

weeks.assessment_key: Critique: names warm and cool colors in their collage and Matisse's, says one feeling. Rhythm check: claps 4 cards (ta, ti-ti, rest) accurately. Proficient = 4/4 cards + uses at least 3 color words (warm, cool, primary, secondary).

weeks.prep: Crayons with paper removed, thin paper, leaves, coins, sandpaper, mesh; xylophone, piano, or free piano app.
misconceptions: Confusing 'high' with 'loud': high/low is pitch; loud/soft is dynamics.
Pressing too hard in rubbings: use the side of the crayon lightly.

days.guide: Touch 10 surfaces at home; describe each texture.

questions.a: How something feels or looks like it would feel.
Rough.

days.guide: Place objects under thin paper; rub with the side of a crayon.

questions.q: Which crayon part do you use?
questions.a: The flat side, with the paper wrapper removed.

days.guide: Play high and low notes; your child reaches up for high, touches toes for low.

questions.q: Is a bird's chirp high or low?
questions.a: High.

days.guide: Sort animal sounds into high (bird, mouse) and low (bear, cow).

questions.q: Is a lion's roar high or low?
questions.a: Low.

days.guide: Display rubbings; family guesses each source.

questions.a: Answers based on rubbings, e.g., bark or mesh.

weeks.assessment_key: Rubbings collection: at least 4 clear rubbings (leaf, coin, mesh, bark or sandpaper) each labeled with a texture word (bumpy, smooth, rough, ridged). Proficient = 4 labeled rubbings + correctly guesses sources.

weeks.prep: Tissue paper, paint, forks, sponges, old combs, paper; 'The Very Hungry Caterpillar' by Eric Carle.
misconceptions: Thinking melody and beat are the same: melody is the tune of notes; beat is the steady pulse.
Thinking Eric Carle drew with crayons: he painted papers and cut them into collage.

days.guide: Read 'The Very Hungry Caterpillar'; look closely at textured painted paper.

questions.q: How did Eric Carle make his pictures?
questions.a: He painted papers with texture and cut them into collage pieces.
A beautiful butterfly.

days.guide: Paint papers; drag forks, press sponges and comb designs for texture. Let dry.

questions.q: What tools did you use for texture?
questions.a: Forks, sponges, combs.

days.guide: Sing 'Jack and Jill' moving hands up, down or same with the notes.

questions.a: A tune; a group of notes going up, down or staying the same.

days.guide: Draw lines for 'Twinkle, Twinkle': up on 'twinkle, twinkle,' then down by steps on 'how I wonder what you are.'

questions.q: Does 'how I wonder what you are' go up or down?
questions.a: Down.

days.guide: Share textured papers and melody chart.

questions.q: Where in 'Twinkle' does the melody jump up?
questions.a: At the second 'twinkle' ('twinkle, TWINKLE').

weeks.assessment_key: Melody direction chart: lines show 'Twinkle, Twinkle' leaping up at 'twinkle, twinkle' and then stepping down on 'how I wonder what you are.' Proficient = chart shows correct up and down direction for both lines.

weeks.prep: Textured papers from last week, glue, scissors; animal photos.
misconceptions: Thinking sol is lower than mi: sol is higher.
Drawing animal details first: start with big shapes.

days.guide: Observe an animal photo; sketch its big shapes (oval body, circle head).

questions.q: What shape is the animal's body?
questions.a: Answers vary, e.g., an oval.

days.guide: Cut and glue textured papers into an Eric Carle-style animal.

questions.a: It adds interest and makes it look like fur, scales or feathers.

days.guide: Teach sol (flat hand) and mi (hand facing chest lower). Sing 'Rain, Rain, Go Away' with signs.

questions.q: Which is higher, sol or mi?
questions.a: Sol.

days.guide: Sing 'Where are you?' (sol-sol-mi); your child creates a call for family to echo.

questions.a: High then low.

days.guide: Present collage animal and sing the sol-mi call.

questions.a: Names textures in the collage.

weeks.assessment_key: Collage animal: built from big shapes cut from textured papers with details added. Sol-mi singing: sings 'Rain, Rain, Go Away' and their own call with sol (higher) and mi (lower) matching hand signs. Proficient = recognizable animal + accurate high-low singing.

weeks.prep: Unit artwork, paper strips in two colors, glockenspiel or piano app; recording of 'Flight of the Bumblebee' (Rimsky-Korsakov).
misconceptions: Weaving every strip the same way: alternate over-under for each new strip.
Playing Hot Cross Buns E-D-C backwards: it goes down from E.

days.guide: Look at a woven basket and a quilt photo; describe textures.

questions.a: Bumpy, ridged, rough.

days.guide: Cut slits in folded paper; weave strips over-under, alternating each row.

questions.q: If row 1 starts 'over,' how does row 2 start?
questions.a: Under.

days.guide: Play 'Hot Cross Buns': E-D-C, E-D-C, C-C-C-C D-D-D-D, E-D-C.

questions.q: What are the first three notes?
questions.a: E, D, C.

days.guide: Listen to 'Flight of the Bumblebee.'

questions.q: Is it fast or slow? High or low?
questions.a: Very fast; mostly high, buzzing notes like a bee.

days.guide: Show weaving; play 'Hot Cross Buns.'

questions.q: Does Hot Cross Buns go up or down at first?
questions.a: Down (E-D-C).

weeks.assessment_key: Weaving: alternating over-under pattern with at least 5 strips. 'Hot Cross Buns': E-D-C, E-D-C, C-C-C-C D-D-D-D, E-D-C. Proficient = correct notes with steady beat + tight over-under weaving.

weeks.prep: Patterned fabric or wrapping paper, markers, paper; lyrics for 'She'll Be Coming 'Round the Mountain.'
misconceptions: Thinking a pattern only repeats once: a pattern repeats again and again.
Calling folk songs 'old pop songs': folk songs are passed down by people, often with unknown composers.

days.guide: Hunt patterns in clothes, floors and wrapping paper; draw three.

questions.a: Something that repeats in order.

days.guide: Make an ABAB border and an ABC border.

questions.q: What comes next: red, blue, red, blue, ___?
questions.a: Red.

questions.q: What comes next in ABC: circle, square, triangle, circle, ___?
questions.a: Square.

days.guide: Sing 'She'll Be Coming 'Round the Mountain' with motions.

questions.a: Each verse repeats its line several times, plus the motions.

days.guide: Explain that this American folk song was sung by workers (such as railroad workers) and passed down; songs help work go faster.

questions.a: A song passed down by people over time; often nobody knows who wrote it.

questions.q: Why did people sing while working?
questions.a: To keep a rhythm together and make work more fun.

days.guide: Explain the border; lead the folk song.

questions.a: Names the repeating units correctly.

weeks.assessment_key: Pattern border: one ABAB border (e.g., star-heart-star-heart) and one ABC border (circle-square-triangle repeated) with no breaks. Proficient = both patterns correct all the way around.

weeks.prep: Corks, bottle caps, sponges, potatoes (adult cuts), paint, paper; a song with verse and chorus ('Jingle Bells').
misconceptions: Thinking verse and chorus are the same: the chorus repeats the same words; verses have new words.
Letting the child carve with a knife: adults carve; child designs and prints.

days.guide: Stamp patterns with corks, bottle caps and sponges.

questions.a: A picture made by pressing a painted object onto paper.

days.guide: Adult carves simple potato stamps; child prints a repeating pattern.

questions.q: Why is a stamp good for patterns?
questions.a: It makes the same shape again and again.

days.guide: Listen to 'Jingle Bells'; raise a hand when the chorus repeats.

questions.q: Which part repeats with the same words?
questions.a: The chorus ('Jingle bells, jingle bells, jingle all the way…').

days.guide: Sing a cumulative song like 'There Was an Old Lady' and notice how each verse adds on.

questions.q: What pattern does the song have?
questions.a: Each verse adds one more thing to the list and repeats the earlier ones.

days.guide: Display prints; identify verse and chorus.

questions.a: A part of the song with new words each time.

weeks.assessment_key: Print: a repeating pattern (at least 2 stamps alternated) on wrapping paper. Verse/chorus: raises hand each time the 'Jingle bells, jingle bells' chorus returns. Proficient = clear repeating print + identifies chorus each time.

weeks.prep: Paper strips, glue or tape; lyrics for 'Dreidel Song,' 'Feliz Navidad,' 'Jingle Bells.'
misconceptions: Thinking everyone celebrates the same holiday: families celebrate many traditions.
Thinking audiences can talk during performances: listen quietly and clap at the end.

days.guide: Learn 'Dreidel Song' (Hanukkah, Jewish tradition) and 'Feliz Navidad' (Christmas song by José Feliciano, Spanish and English).

questions.q: What holiday is the Dreidel Song connected to?
questions.a: Hanukkah.
Merry Christmas (in Spanish).

days.guide: Make a patterned paper chain (ABAB colors).

questions.a: Names the repeating colors.

days.guide: Find art made at home for celebrations (cards, ornaments, decorations).

questions.q: Name art people make for celebrations.
questions.a: Cards, decorations, paper chains, ornaments.

days.guide: Rehearse songs for a family sing-along.

questions.a: To learn the words and sing well together.

days.guide: Perform; model audience manners.

questions.q: What does a good audience do?
questions.a: Sits quietly, watches, and claps at the end.

weeks.assessment_key: Sing-along: sings 2-3 songs with correct words, steady beat and expression; shows audience manners when others perform (quiet, eyes on performer, clap at end). Proficient = all.

weeks.prep: Prints from week 15, paper, glue; instruments.
misconceptions: Thinking AB patterns only use two sounds: A and B can be groups of sounds (clap-clap / pat).
Thinking art only happens in lessons: people make art everywhere.

days.guide: Glue printed patterns into a paper-quilt square.

questions.q: What pattern is in your quilt square?
questions.a: Names a repeating pattern.

days.guide: Create an AB pattern (A = clap-clap, B = pat) and repeat 4 times.

questions.q: What comes after A in an AB pattern?
questions.a: B.

days.guide: Perform the body pattern while showing the quilt square.

questions.q: How are your quilt and pattern alike?
questions.a: Both repeat in order.

days.guide: Tell where you make art outside lessons.

questions.q: Where else do you make art?
questions.a: Birthday cards, chalk drawings, decorations.

days.guide: Hold a mini-show of prints and patterns.

questions.q: Which piece are you most proud of?
questions.a: Any with a reason.

weeks.assessment_key: Unit 4 portfolio: pattern border, prints, paper chain, quilt square showing repeating patterns. Body pattern: performs AB pattern (e.g., clap-clap-pat) 4 times steadily. Proficient = complete portfolio + steady pattern.

weeks.prep: Paper strips, tape; access to a Classics for Kids or PBS instrument-family video; instrument pictures.
misconceptions: Thinking a drawing of a ball is a form: drawings are flat shapes; forms are 3-D.
Putting the saxophone in brass: it's metal but a woodwind (uses a reed).

days.guide: Compare a drawn circle with a real ball; find 5 forms (box, can, ball, cone).

questions.q: What is the difference between shape and form?
questions.a: A shape is flat (2-D); a form is 3-D and you can hold or walk around it.

days.guide: Fold, curl and tape paper strips into a standing sculpture.

questions.q: Is your sculpture a shape or a form?
questions.a: A form (3-D).

days.guide: Watch a video about strings, brass, woodwinds and percussion.

questions.q: How do you play percussion instruments?
questions.a: Hit, shake or scrape them.

days.guide: Sort instrument pictures into families.

questions.a: Brass.
Strings.

days.guide: Present sculpture; name the 4 families.

questions.a: Strings, woodwinds, brass, percussion.

weeks.assessment_key: Instrument sort: Strings - violin, viola, cello, double bass, harp; Woodwinds - flute, clarinet, oboe, bassoon (saxophone); Brass - trumpet, French horn, trombone, tuba; Percussion - drums, xylophone, cymbals, triangle, timpani. Proficient = 10+ correct and names all four families.

weeks.prep: Air-dry clay, toothpicks, plastic knife, recording of Prokofiev's 'Peter and the Wolf' (with narration).
misconceptions: Pinching walls too thin: keep walls about as thick as a finger.
Thinking each character is played by any instrument: each has a specific instrument.

days.guide: Show clay tools; roll a smooth ball between palms. Keep clay covered when not used.

questions.q: How do you keep clay from drying?
questions.a: Cover it with plastic or a damp cloth.

days.guide: Press a thumb into the ball, pinch and turn to make walls. Add texture with a toothpick.

questions.q: How do you make a pinch pot?
questions.a: Push a thumb into a ball of clay, then pinch and turn to thin the walls.

days.guide: Listen to 'Peter and the Wolf'; match each instrument to its character.

questions.a: Flute.
French horns.

days.guide: Draw each character with its instrument.

questions.a: Clarinet.

days.guide: Show the pot; retell the story by instruments.

questions.a: Bassoon.
Oboe.

weeks.assessment_key: Matching key: Bird = flute; Duck = oboe; Cat = clarinet; Grandfather = bassoon; Wolf = French horns; Peter = string instruments; Hunters = woodwinds with timpani and bass drum for the shots. Proficient = 5+ correct.

weeks.prep: Boxes, tubes, bottle caps, rubber bands, beans, containers, tape, glue.
misconceptions: Thinking all instruments sound the same: timbre is the special 'color' of each sound.
Rubber bands too loose on a guitar: stretch them tighter for a clearer, higher sound.

days.guide: Sketch a robot or creature from recycled parts.

questions.a: Art made from things that would be thrown away.

days.guide: Assemble with tape and glue.

questions.a: A sculpture made by putting found objects together.

days.guide: Build a drum, shaker or rubber-band guitar.

questions.q: How does a rubber-band guitar make sound?
questions.a: The rubber bands vibrate when plucked.

days.guide: Describe sounds: rattly, booming, twangy.

questions.a: The special sound quality of an instrument or voice.

days.guide: Present the sculpture; play the instrument.

questions.q: What word describes your instrument's sound?
questions.a: Example: 'rattly' for a bean shaker.

weeks.assessment_key: Presentation: sculpture built from recycled parts that stands on its own; instrument makes sound; child uses a timbre word (rattly, booming, twangy). Proficient = all three.

weeks.prep: Photos of the Statue of Liberty and local sculptures; sketchbook; homemade instruments.
misconceptions: Thinking art only lives in museums: public art is in parks, streets and buildings.
Everyone playing at once in solos: wait for your 4-beat turn.

days.guide: Look at the Statue of Liberty and other public sculptures.

questions.q: What does the Statue of Liberty stand for?
questions.a: Freedom; it welcomed people arriving in New York.

days.guide: Walk in your community; sketch a piece of public art.

questions.a: Answers vary: murals, statues, fountains.

days.guide: Play homemade instruments together on a steady beat.

questions.a: A group performing music together.

days.guide: Each instrument plays a 4-beat solo in turn.

questions.a: When one person plays alone.

days.guide: Explain why sculptures are placed in public.

questions.q: Why put sculptures in public places?
questions.a: To honor people or events, make places beautiful, and let everyone enjoy art.

weeks.assessment_key: Ensemble: plays homemade instruments with family on a steady beat and takes a 4-beat solo at the right time. Proficient = steady beat and correct solo entry.

weeks.prep: Air-dry clay, paint for later; recordings of 6 instruments (violin, flute, trumpet, drum, piano, guitar).
misconceptions: Attaching clay pieces without scoring: scratch and add a little water ('score and slip') so pieces stick.
Guessing by look not sound: listen with eyes closed.

days.guide: Sculpt an animal using pinch and coil techniques; score and slip to join.

questions.q: How do you make a coil?
questions.a: Roll clay back and forth into a long snake.

days.guide: Add details; let dry; paint when dry.

questions.q: Why let clay dry before painting?
questions.a: Paint sticks better and the clay won't smudge.

days.guide: Play 6 instrument sounds; your child names each.

questions.q: A low, rumbling string sound is probably?
questions.a: Cello or double bass.

days.guide: Create a short sound story using different instruments for characters.

questions.q: Which instrument is your main character?
questions.a: Names instrument chosen.

days.guide: Show clay animal; perform sound story.

questions.q: Why give each character a different instrument?
questions.a: So listeners can tell who is in the story by the sound.

weeks.assessment_key: Listening quiz (6 instruments by sound): answers depend on clips played; record child's identifications against your key. Sound story: different instrument for each character, clear beginning-middle-end. Proficient = 5/6 + complete story.

weeks.prep: Tissue paper, scissors; photos of papel picado; mariachi recording; lyrics to 'De Colores' or 'La Cucaracha.'
misconceptions: Cutting along the open edge: cut shapes on folded edges to make symmetric holes.
Thinking mariachi is only trumpets: mariachi uses violins, trumpets, guitars, vihuela and guitarrón.

days.guide: Look at papel picado; explain it is a Mexican folk art used for celebrations.

questions.q: When do people hang papel picado?
questions.a: At celebrations: Día de los Muertos, holidays, weddings, birthdays, fiestas.

days.guide: Fold tissue paper several times; cut small shapes on the folds; unfold.

questions.a: Perforated (cut) paper.

days.guide: Listen to mariachi music; name the instruments.

questions.a: Violin, trumpet, guitar, vihuela, guitarrón.

days.guide: Learn 'De Colores' or 'La Cucaracha.'

questions.q: What language is the song in?
questions.a: Spanish.

days.guide: Explain why people make papel picado.

questions.a: To decorate and celebrate special days in Mexican culture.

weeks.assessment_key: Papel picado: folded tissue banner with cut shapes; child explains use (celebrations such as Día de los Muertos, holidays, weddings). Song: sings 'De Colores' or 'La Cucaracha' chorus. Proficient = banner + explanation + song.

weeks.prep: Image of Hokusai's 'The Great Wave off Kanagawa,' blue paint, white and black; koto music recording; 'Sakura' recording.
misconceptions: Thinking 'The Great Wave' is a painting: it is a woodblock print.
Thinking the koto is a guitar: it is a long Japanese zither played lying flat.

days.guide: Look at Hokusai's 'The Great Wave'; describe curling lines, white foam, blue colors, boats, Mount Fuji.

questions.q: What mountain is in the background?
questions.a: Mount Fuji.
As a woodblock print in Japan.

days.guide: Paint a wave using blue tints and shades.

questions.q: How do you make light blue?
questions.a: Add white (a tint).

days.guide: Listen to koto music; describe its sound.

questions.a: By plucking its strings while it lies flat.

days.guide: Learn 'Sakura.'

questions.a: Cherry blossoms.

days.guide: Explain why museums keep 'The Great Wave' safe.

questions.a: It's old paper; light and handling can fade and damage it, and it's important to people.

weeks.assessment_key: Wave painting uses blue tints and shades. Listening response: koto described as plucked strings, gentle/twangy; 'Sakura' melody slow, calm, about cherry blossoms. Proficient = 3+ blues and accurate descriptions.

weeks.prep: Paper strips in gold (yellow), green, red and black; images of kente cloth; bucket or drum; 'Funga Alafia' recording.
misconceptions: Thinking kente colors are random: each color has meaning.
Answering before the call ends: wait for the leader, then respond.

days.guide: Look at kente cloth from Ghana; learn color meanings.

questions.q: Where does kente cloth come from?
questions.a: Ghana in West Africa.

questions.q: What does gold mean in kente?
questions.a: Wealth, royalty, high status.

days.guide: Weave gold, green, red and black strips over-under; glue ends.

questions.a: Growth, harvest, new life.

days.guide: Play call-and-response rhythms on a bucket like a djembe.

questions.a: A leader plays or sings a part and the group answers.

days.guide: Sing 'Funga Alafia' with welcoming motions.

questions.q: What kind of song is 'Funga Alafia'?
questions.a: A West African welcome song.

days.guide: Present weaving; lead a call-and-response.

questions.a: For special occasions; it shows pride and meaning.

weeks.assessment_key: Kente weaving: alternating strips in gold, green, red, black glued at ends. Child names one meaning (gold = wealth/royalty; green = growth/harvest; red = sacrifice/strength; black = maturity/ancestors). Call-and-response: echoes leader and leads one call. Proficient = all.

weeks.prep: Photos of Pomo baskets (Calisphere), paper plate cut as loom, yarn; recording of a California Native song.
misconceptions: Thinking Native art is only in the past: California Native peoples still make baskets and sing today.
Thinking baskets were only decoration: they were used for cooking, storing, carrying and ceremonies.

days.guide: Look at Pomo basket photos; discuss why they are valued.

questions.a: A Native people of Northern California known for fine baskets.
They are tightly and beautifully woven, sometimes with feathers and shells; they carry tradition.

days.guide: Weave yarn on a paper-plate loom.

questions.a: Going over and under to make a fabric or basket.

days.guide: Listen to a California Native song; describe the beat.

questions.a: Usually yes, often a drum or rattle keeps it.

days.guide: Compare art and music from Mexico, Japan, West Africa and California Native peoples.

questions.q: How are these cultures' art alike?
questions.a: All create art to celebrate, tell stories and use in daily life.

days.guide: Present a favorite artwork from another culture and explain why people made it.

questions.a: Accurate reason, e.g., papel picado to celebrate.

weeks.assessment_key: Cultural comparison: child presents a favorite artwork from Mexico, Japan, West Africa or California Native peoples and explains why people made it (celebration, telling stories, everyday use, honoring tradition). Proficient = names culture, describes work and gives an accurate reason.

weeks.prep: Watercolors, brushes, paper; Haydn's 'Surprise Symphony' (Symphony No. 94, 2nd movement).
misconceptions: Thinking 'piano' only means the instrument: in music it also means soft.
Drawing the horizon at the very top: it is where sky meets land, often in the middle.

days.guide: Sketch the window view: sky, horizon, ground.

questions.a: The line where the sky seems to meet the land or sea.

days.guide: Paint the landscape with watercolors (sky first, then ground).

questions.a: A picture of outdoor scenery.

days.guide: Listen to the 'Surprise Symphony'; jump at the loud chord.

questions.a: Quiet music suddenly had a very loud chord.

days.guide: Sing softly (piano) and loudly (forte) on cue.

questions.a: Loud.
Soft.

days.guide: Explain your landscape and why Haydn used a surprise.

questions.q: Why did Haydn add a surprise?
questions.a: To wake up and surprise the audience and make the music exciting.

weeks.assessment_key: Landscape: shows sky, horizon line and ground. Dynamics: sings softly (piano) and loudly (forte) on cue. Proficient = horizon visible + correct responses to cues.

weeks.prep: Image of Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night,' oil pastels, dark paper; recording of Grieg's 'In the Hall of the Mountain King.'
misconceptions: Thinking tempo means loudness: tempo is speed.
Blending oil pastels too much: show visible swirl strokes like Van Gogh.

days.guide: Look at 'The Starry Night'; trace swirling lines in the air.

questions.a: Swirling sky, bright stars, a crescent moon, a village, a tall dark cypress tree.

days.guide: Draw a swirling night sky with oil pastels.

questions.a: The mark a brush (or tool) leaves.

days.guide: Listen to 'In the Hall of the Mountain King'; move as it speeds up.

questions.a: It starts slow and quiet and gets faster and louder.

days.guide: Sing 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat' slow, then fast.

questions.a: How fast or slow music goes.

days.guide: Explain how tempo changed the mood.

questions.q: How did the fast part feel?
questions.a: Exciting, scary, rushed.

weeks.assessment_key: Night sky drawing shows swirling lines and bright stars. Tempo response: moves slowly at the start of 'Mountain King' and faster as it speeds up. Proficient = swirls + matching movement.

weeks.prep: Saint-Saëns 'Carnival of the Animals' recording ('Royal March of the Lion,' 'The Elephant,' 'The Swan,' 'Aquarium'), paints.
misconceptions: Thinking only words tell stories: music can describe animals with tempo, dynamics and instruments.
Giving opinions without reasons: say 'I like it because…'.

days.guide: Listen to 'Royal March of the Lion' and 'The Elephant.'

questions.q: How does the elephant music sound?
questions.a: Slow, low and heavy (played by the double bass).

days.guide: Listen to 'The Swan' and 'Aquarium'; describe the mood.

questions.a: Cello.
Calm, smooth and graceful.

days.guide: Paint an animal while its music plays.

questions.a: Names the animal.

days.guide: Choose a favorite movement and explain why.

questions.a: Camille Saint-Saëns.

days.guide: Act out animals as the music plays.

questions.q: How would you move to the elephant music?
questions.a: Slowly and heavily.

weeks.assessment_key: Listening responses with reasons: Lion - grand march with roaring runs (piano/strings); Elephant - slow, heavy, low double bass; Swan - slow, smooth, graceful cello; Aquarium - shimmering, flowing, mysterious. Proficient = describes 3 with tempo/dynamics/instrument words and gives reasons.

weeks.prep: A fresh flower, magnifier; image of a Georgia O'Keeffe flower painting; Vivaldi's 'Spring' from The Four Seasons.
misconceptions: Thinking big art must be of big things: O'Keeffe painted small flowers huge so people would notice.
Drawing the flower small in the middle: fill the page.

days.guide: Look at an O'Keeffe flower painting; notice how large it is.

questions.q: Why did O'Keeffe paint flowers so big?
questions.a: So people would stop and really look at them.

days.guide: Observe a flower with a magnifier; draw it large to fill the page.

questions.a: Veins, center parts, colors.

days.guide: Listen to Vivaldi's 'Spring'; identify bird sounds and the storm.

questions.q: Which instrument makes the bird sounds?
questions.a: Violins.

questions.q: How does the storm part sound?
questions.a: Fast, loud, rumbling notes.

days.guide: Compare how O'Keeffe and Vivaldi show nature.

questions.a: Both show nature: O'Keeffe with paint, Vivaldi with sound.

days.guide: Explain your flower drawing choices.

questions.a: A view very near the subject so it looks big.

weeks.assessment_key: Close-up flower drawing: fills the page, shows petal details seen through magnifier. Proficient = drawing fills page + child explains choices (size, color, details).

weeks.prep: Paper (4 panels), crayons, instruments.
misconceptions: Ignoring feedback: one suggestion can make work better.
Using the same sound for every panel: change tempo and dynamics to match the mood.

days.guide: Plan a 4-panel nature story: storm, sun, birds, night.

questions.a: Describes the 4 panels in order.

days.guide: Draw the panels using warm or cool colors to match mood.

questions.q: What colors suit the night panel?
questions.a: Cool colors like blue and purple.

days.guide: Add instruments, dynamics and tempo for each panel.

questions.a: Loud and fast.

days.guide: Perform; revise based on one suggestion.

questions.a: Names a specific change.

days.guide: Perform the revised story.

questions.a: To change and improve your work.

weeks.assessment_key: Sound story rubric: 4 panels (storm, sun, birds, night) with matching warm/cool colors; instruments, dynamics and tempo match each panel; revised using one suggestion. 4 = all; 3 = minor gap; 2 = missing panel or sound; 1 = incomplete.

weeks.prep: All artwork from the year, a folder; list of songs learned.
misconceptions: Choosing only the newest work: choose work you're proudest of or that shows learning.
Saying 'I like it' without why: give a reason.

days.guide: Lay out all art in order; sort by medium.

questions.a: The material used: paint, crayon, clay, paper, print.

days.guide: Choose 6 favorites; tell why for each.

questions.q: Why did you choose this one?
questions.a: Specific reason using art words.

days.guide: Choose 3 favorite songs for a spring concert.

questions.a: Names 3 songs.

days.guide: Rehearse with expression (dynamics, tempo).

questions.q: How can you sing with expression?
questions.a: Change loud/soft and fast/slow to fit the words.

days.guide: Explain choices for art and songs.

questions.a: A collection of your best work.

weeks.assessment_key: Portfolio selection: 6 artworks with a reason for each (e.g., 'I used warm colors,' 'I worked hard on texture'). Proficient = 6 pieces from at least 3 media with specific reasons.

weeks.prep: Construction paper for mats, labels, pencil; instruments.
misconceptions: Putting labels that only say the title: include title, medium and artist.
Practicing only easy parts: fix tricky parts.

days.guide: Mount art on colored paper mats with a border.

questions.q: Why put art on a mat?
questions.a: To frame it and make it look finished.

days.guide: Write labels: title, medium, artist name.

questions.q: What goes on a museum label?
questions.a: Title, medium, artist name.

days.guide: Rehearse songs; fix tricky parts with feedback.

questions.q: What part was tricky? How did you fix it?
questions.a: Specific answer.

days.guide: Add a shaker on the beat and a drum on a ta/ti-ti rhythm.

questions.q: Does the shaker play the beat or the rhythm?
questions.a: The beat.

days.guide: Practice explaining one artwork to a visitor.

questions.q: What would you tell a visitor?
questions.a: Title, how it was made, and an idea or feeling.

weeks.assessment_key: Labels: each shows Title, Medium (e.g., tempera paint, collage), Artist name. Rehearsal: one tricky part improved; shaker on beat and drum on ta/ti-ti rhythm. Proficient = complete labels + steady instrument parts.

weeks.prep: Virtual tour of the National Gallery of Art or the Met (online); paper for floor plan.
misconceptions: Thinking a curator makes the art: a curator chooses and cares for art; a docent gives tours.
Clapping during a song: wait until it ends.

days.guide: Take a virtual museum tour; discuss curators and docents.

questions.a: Chooses, cares for and arranges art in a museum.
Gives tours and explains the art.

days.guide: Draw a floor plan of where 6 artworks will hang and why.

questions.q: Why put art at eye level?
questions.a: So visitors can see it easily.

days.guide: Practice audience and performer etiquette.

questions.q: What does a performer do at the end?
questions.a: Bows.
Listens quietly and claps at the end.

days.guide: Full concert rehearsal.

questions.a: A practice of the whole show just like the real one.

days.guide: Act as docent for 3 artworks.

questions.a: The people watching or listening.

weeks.assessment_key: Docent practice: 2-minute tour of 3 artworks naming materials and an idea for each; speaks clearly and faces audience. Proficient = 3 artworks with materials + ideas.

weeks.prep: Matted, labeled art; tape; invitation paper; instruments.
misconceptions: Rushing the concert: breathe and keep a steady tempo.
Talking only about mistakes when reflecting: name strengths too.

days.guide: Hang artworks at child eye level following the plan.

questions.a: To place each artwork where you planned.

days.guide: Make invitations with pattern borders.

questions.q: What information goes on an invitation?
questions.a: What, when, where, who.

days.guide: Host the art show; act as docent.

questions.a: A public show of art.

days.guide: Perform 3 songs with instruments.

questions.q: How do you start a performance?
questions.a: Stand ready, wait for quiet, then begin.

days.guide: Reflect: proud and different.

questions.a: Specific answer.

weeks.assessment_key: Art show and concert: art hung at child eye level with labels; child gives tours; performs 3 songs with instruments. Reflection names one proud moment and one change. Proficient = all.

weeks.prep: A September and May drawing, first and latest rhythm compositions, a new sketchbook, music access.
misconceptions: Thinking growth means perfection: growth is improving over time.
Thinking art stops in summer: keep a sketchbook.

days.guide: Compare a September and May drawing; note growth.

questions.a: Examples: more details, more colors, fills the page.

days.guide: Compare first rhythm with latest composition.

questions.q: What new note did you add since September?
questions.a: Ti-ti and the quarter rest; longer 8-beat rhythms.

days.guide: Start a summer sketchbook with 3 prompts.

questions.a: Example: draw your favorite place using warm colors.

days.guide: Make a playlist of favorite pieces.

questions.q: Name a piece from your playlist.
questions.a: Example: 'Carnival of the Animals.'

days.guide: Share growth and summer plan; sing a favorite song together.

questions.q: What is your favorite thing you learned?
questions.a: Specific answer.

weeks.assessment_key: Reflection: names 2 specific changes between early and late work (more detail, more colors, filled page, steadier rhythm), sets 3 sketchbook prompts and names favorite songs. Proficient = specific growth comparisons.
